info.description:
## Welcome to the Zebracat AI Public API

Zebracat gives you a full suite of **agentic video generation** tools you can plug into any workflow, any platform, anywhere. Generate complete videos end-to-end, or use individual building blocks — **AI image generation**, **music generation**, **voice-over synthesis**, **AI avatars**, **video cloning**, **video translation**, and more — as standalone APIs.

Build text-to-video, blog-to-video, idea-to-video pipelines, or mix and match our tools to create something entirely your own.

### Base URL

All API endpoints are served under the versioned base path:

```
https://api.zebracat.ai/api/v1/public/
```

### API Versioning

The Zebracat API uses **URL-based versioning**. The version is included in the URL path (e.g. `/api/v1/public/...`).

- **Current version:** `v1`
- **Version header:** Every response includes an `API-Version` header with the version used.
- **Unversioned alias:** `/api/public/` maps to the latest stable version (currently v1).
- **Deprecation policy:** Older versions will be supported for at least 6 months after a new version is released. Deprecation timelines will be announced via the changelog and response headers.

### Authentication

Zebracat supports **two** ways to authenticate, each billed from a different pool:

1. **API key (`X-API-KEY`)** — pay-as-you-go, billed from your **API dollar balance**. Best for servers, CI and scripts. Generate a key at [zebracat.ai/api](https://zebracat.ai/api) and send it on every request:
   ```
   X-API-KEY: sk-your-api-key-here
   ```
2. **OAuth 2.1 (`Authorization: Bearer …`)** — log in with your Zebracat account and spend your **normal plan credits** (no separate top-up). Best for end-user apps, the Zebracat CLI (`zebracat auth login`) and MCP clients (Claude Code, Cursor). Discovery: `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`; the flow is standard authorization-code + PKCE with dynamic client registration at `POST /api/oauth/register`.

### ID types cheat-sheet

Different resources use different identifier formats — send the right one:

| Field | Format | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| `voice_id` | provider string (e.g. `21m00Tcm4TlvDq8ikWAM`) | `GET /voices` — or one of **your cloned voices** from `GET /voice/clone` |
| `style_id` (visual style) | integer | `GET /visual_styles` |
| `avatar_id` / `brand_id` / `character_id` | integer | `GET /avatars` / `GET /brands` / `GET /characters` |
| `language` (generation) | lowercase English name (`english`, `spanish`) | `GET /video/languages` |
| `target_language` (translation) | ISO 639-1 code (`es`) or name | `GET /video/translate/languages` |
| `task_id` | hex string from any create call | create responses / `GET /videos` |
| `project_id` | integer | create responses — open at `https://studio.zebracat.ai/storyboard/{project_id}` |

### Error handling

Every error uses one envelope. `error` is always present; `type` (the family: `invalid_request`, `authentication`, `permission`, `insufficient_funds`, `not_found`, `conflict`, `rate_limited`, `engine`, `unavailable`), `retryable` and `request_id` are added on every error, and the other keys appear when known. Every code is listed in the [Errors guide](/docs/guides/errors.md):

```json
{
  "error": "mood must be one of hype_swagger, energetic_upbeat, ... .",
  "code": "invalid_choice",
  "field": "mood",
  "allowed_values": ["hype_swagger", "energetic_upbeat", "motivational_inspiring", "cinematic_storytelling", "suspense_mysterious", "curious_intriguing", "emotional_sad", "calm_chill", "happy_feelgood", "funny_quirky"],
  "hint": "optional actionable next step",
  "errors": [{"...": "every problem found, when more than one"}]
}
```

Common `code` values: `missing_field`, `invalid_choice`, `invalid_type`, `not_found`, `unknown_field` (unrecognized body key — the `hint` says where it belongs), `duration_over_plan`, `url_unreachable`, `file_too_large`, `invalid_media`, `insufficient_balance` / `insufficient_credit` (402, with `topup_url`/`billing_url`), `concurrency_limit` / `daily_quota` (429), `project_setup_failed`.

Unknown body fields are **rejected** (HTTP 400, `code: unknown_field`) with a hint — e.g. sending `video_type` to `/video/idea` explains that only `/video/agentic` accepts it and that this endpoint wants `footage_type` instead.

### Making a video

Video generation is **asynchronous** and runs the same engine as the dashboard's chat:

1. **Submit** `POST /videos` with a `brief` (and any structured choices). You get `202` with a `task_id` and a `phase`. With `auto_generate: false` the video stops at `plan_ready` so you can read the plan, change it and see its exact price (`GET /videos/{task_id}/quote`) before `POST /videos/{task_id}/generate`.
2. **Track it**: poll `GET /videos/{task_id}` until `phase` is `completed` (or `failed`), or register a webhook (`POST /webhooks`) for `video.plan_ready`, `video.completed`, `video.failed` and the rest.
3. **Get the result**: `video_url` is the MP4; every project also opens in the editor at `https://studio.zebracat.ai/storyboard/{project_id}`.

Every call that can spend money accepts `"dry_run": true` and answers its price instead; every create accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header. The v1 endpoints (`/video/idea`, `/video/script`, …) keep working.

- [Agent quickstart](/docs/guides/agent-quickstart.md): one call to a finished video

### For AI agents

- **[`/docs/llms.txt`](/docs/llms.txt)**: the llmstxt.org index of these docs; **[`/docs/llms-full.txt`](/docs/llms-full.txt)**: every guide and the whole reference in one Markdown file. Both are generated from this schema and the code.
- **Per-group reference in Markdown:** `/docs/reference/<group>.md`.
- **MCP server:** `https://mcp.zebracat.ai/mcp` (OAuth or X-API-KEY): see the MCP guide.
- **Postman:** [`/docs/postman.json`](/docs/postman.json), a Postman Collection v2.1 of this API.
- **OpenAPI 3.1:** [`/docs/openapi.json`](/docs/openapi.json).

### Pricing

API usage is billed per request based on your plan — `GET /pricing` returns live per-service prices. Visit [zebracat.ai/api](https://zebracat.ai/api) to view pricing and choose the plan that fits your needs.

### Support

Need help? Reach out to us at [zebracat.ai](https://zebracat.ai) or check our documentation for guides and examples.

Returns the authenticated account, its subscription plan, and **both** credit pools:

- `account_credit` — your subscription/plan credit, spent when you authenticate via **OAuth** (browser login / the Zebracat CLI `zebracat auth login`).
- `api_dollar_balance` — pay-as-you-go dollars, spent when you authenticate with an **X-API-KEY**.

Returns all active (non-deleted) API keys for the authenticated user, newest first. Takes no parameters.

Each key in the array includes:
- `api_key` — The key value, used in the `X-API-KEY` header (format `sk-...`)
- `name` — Optional label set at creation
- `usage` — Total dollars spent through this key
- `dollar_balance` — The account's shared API dollar balance (same across all keys)
- `is_active` — Whether the key can authenticate requests

Note: only active, non-deleted keys are returned; soft-deleted keys are omitted.

**Request body (all optional):**

post.description:
Create your custom avatar (digital twin) from a photo or a short video.

- **`image_url`** — the photo becomes the avatar immediately (`status: finished`). It is animated and lip-synced automatically whenever you use it in a video (`avatar_id` on `POST /video/agentic`).
- **`video_url`** — the first clean frame is extracted server-side; the avatar returns as `processing` — poll `GET /avatars/clone/{avatar_id}` until `finished`.

Exactly one of `image_url` / `video_url` is required. The face should be clearly visible, front-facing, and well lit.

image_url.description: Public https URL of a photo (JPG/PNG/WebP). The photo becomes the avatar.

video_url.description: Public https URL of a short video; the first clean frame becomes the avatar.

200.description: Avatar created (image path: finished; video path: processing).

get.description:
## Zebracat MCP Server

The Zebracat MCP (Model Context Protocol) Server lets you connect AI-powered tools like **Claude Desktop**, **Claude Code**, **Cursor**, **Windsurf**, and any MCP-compatible client directly to Zebracat's video generation API.

### What You Can Do

- **Generate videos** from ideas, scripts, blog URLs, or audio files
- **Translate videos** into 27+ languages
- **Browse assets** — voices, avatars, visual styles, templates
- **Check status** of video generation tasks
- **Monitor balance** and API usage

### Quick Start

1. Get your API key from [zebracat.ai/api](https://zebracat.ai/api)
2. Connect using one of the methods below
3. Start generating videos through natural language

---

#### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http zebracat https://mcp.zebracat.ai/mcp/ \
  --header "X-API-KEY: sk-your-api-key"
```

#### Claude Desktop

Add to your config file (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` on macOS or `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json` on Windows):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zebracat": {
      "url": "https://mcp.zebracat.ai/mcp/",
      "headers": {
        "X-API-KEY": "sk-your-api-key"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

#### Cursor

1. Open Cursor Settings > MCP
2. Click **Add new MCP server**
3. Set type to **HTTP** and URL to `https://mcp.zebracat.ai/mcp/`
4. Add header `X-API-KEY: sk-your-api-key`

#### Windsurf

Add to your Windsurf MCP config (`~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "zebracat": {
      "serverUrl": "https://mcp.zebracat.ai/mcp/",
      "headers": {
        "X-API-KEY": "sk-your-api-key"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Authentication

All requests require your Zebracat API key in the `X-API-KEY` header. Get your key from [zebracat.ai/api](https://zebracat.ai/api). The same key works for both the REST API and MCP.

### Example Prompts

Once connected, try these with your AI assistant:

- *"Create a 30-second video about the benefits of remote work"*
- *"Generate a video from this blog post: https://example.com/article"*
- *"Show me available voices in English"*
- *"What visual styles are available?"*
- *"Check the status of my latest video"*

Returns all available preset templates.

Each template includes an `is_allowed` field. It is now always `true` — every template is available to every user — and is kept so existing integrations that read it keep parsing.

**Template categories:**
- `ai` — AI-generated video templates
- `stock` — Stock footage-based templates
- `sketch` — Sketch/illustration-style templates
- `infinite_zoom` — Infinite zoom effect templates

**Filtering by category:**
Use `?category=ai` to filter templates by category.

**Response fields:**
- `id` — Template ID
- `name` — Template name
- `category` — Template category (`ai`, `stock`, `sketch`, `infinite_zoom`)
- `footage_type` — Type of footage used
- `aspect_ratio` — Video aspect ratio
- `preview` — Video preview URL
- `thumbnail_src` — Thumbnail image URL
- `is_allowed` — Always `true`; templates are no longer plan-gated
- `voice_id` — Default voice ID
- `region` — Template language

**Deprecated fields** (kept for backwards compatibility, always the same value):
- `attributes` — always `{}`. Presentation now comes from the brand kit.
- `has_caption` — always `true`. Captions are always on.
- `character_consistency` — always `true`. Now a pipeline default.
- `voice_provider`, `is_premium_voice` — derived from `voice_id`.
- `mood` — always `happy`. Mood is expressed in the template's prompt.

Templates are prompt-first: use `GET /api/user/templates` for the prompt markup, its parsed segments and the video's own prompt.

post.description:
Submit a prompt and let the AI agent decide the best video type, visual style, mood, voice, aspect ratio, and all production parameters automatically.

The agent follows this pipeline:
1. Detects input type (idea, URL, or script)
2. Uses LLM to recommend video type, visual style, mood, and prompt style
3. Picks the best voice using score-based matching
4. Determines aspect ratio from context keywords
5. Builds a complete video plan and starts generation

You can optionally override any of the agent's decisions by providing explicit values for `video_type`, `duration`, `language`, `mood`, `visual_style`, `aspect_ratio`, or `voice_id`.

**Credit:** An AVPC (Agentic Video Plan Cost) credit is charged for the AI planning step. Additional generation credits are charged during rendering.

Use the returned `task_id` to poll status via `GET /api/public/video/status`.

- A free-text idea (e.g. 'A video about the benefits of meditation')
- A blog/article URL (e.g. 'https://example.com/article')

Create a new video modeled on an existing one (the dashboard's *copy-a-video* flow).

This starts an **asynchronous** job and returns immediately with a `task_id` and `project_id`. The pipeline then:
1. Analyzes the reference video (visual style, pacing, structure, script, music, mood)
2. Plans a new video with the same agent the dashboard chat uses — measured reference properties (video type, style, duration, voice tone) drive the plan
3. Writes the script per `mode`, synthesizes the voice-over, generates visuals
4. Optionally renders the final MP4 (only when `should_render` is `true`)

- `remix` (default) — same structure and energy, your `topic` (or an auto-derived one)
- `generate_similar` — the reference recreated closely: same story, cast, places and shots, new wording
- `recreate_script` — re-uses the reference's own transcript verbatim as the script

Either a public post link (TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube / Shorts, Facebook, X, Vimeo…) or a directly-downloadable https media URL (MP4/MOV/WebM). Generate a video from a ready-made voice-over script you provide.

Unlike `idea_to_video` (where you pass a short prompt and the pipeline writes the script for you), here your `script` text is used as the voice-over **verbatim** — it is narrated exactly as written.

This starts an **asynchronous** job and returns immediately with a `task_id` and `project_id`. The pipeline then:
1. Synthesizes the voice-over audio from your script (read word-for-word)
2. Generates AI visuals (or selects stock footage) matching the script
3. Optionally renders the final MP4 (only when `should_render` is `true`)

**Required:** `script`, `language`, `duration`. Everything else is optional (see fields below).

script.description: Required. The full voice-over script the video narrates **verbatim** — this exact text is read aloud, word-for-word, so write it as finished narration (not a prompt or outline). Keep its length roughly in line with `duration` (about 2-3 spoken words per second).

First, protect the first hour: no email, no chat, just one focused task. Next, batch your meetings into a single afternoon block so mornings stay clear. Do this for one week, and you will reclaim hours you did not know you had.

get.description:
Returns all webhooks for the authenticated user.

Each webhook includes:
- `url` — The endpoint that receives POST requests
- `secret` — HMAC-SHA256 signing secret for verifying incoming payloads
- `events` — List of subscribed event types (empty = all events)
- `is_active` — Whether the webhook is currently enabled

**Available event types:**
- `video.completed` — Fired when a video finishes rendering
- `video.failed` — Fired when a video render fails
- `project.created` — Fired when a new project is created
- `project.updated` — Fired when a project is updated
- `credit.low` — Fired when credit balance drops below threshold

---

## Webhook payload structure

When an event fires, a **POST** request is sent to your URL with:

**Headers:**
- `Content-Type: application/json`
- `X-Webhook-Signature` — HMAC-SHA256 hex digest of the raw request body, signed with your webhook `secret`
- `X-Webhook-Event` — The event type string (e.g. `video.completed`)

**Body format:** Every webhook POST body is a JSON object with two top-level keys:

| Field | Type | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ----------- |
| `event` | string | The event type (e.g. `video.completed`) |
| `data` | object | Event-specific payload (see below) |

---

### `video.completed`

Fired when a video finishes rendering successfully.

| `data` field | Type | Description |
| ------------ | ---- | ----------- |
| `task_id` | string | The task ID returned when the video was submitted |
| `video_type` | string | One of: `idea`, `script`, `blog`, `audio`, `translate` |
| `video_url` | string | Public download URL for the rendered video (MP4) |

```json
{
  "event": "video.completed",
  "data": {
    "task_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
    "video_type": "idea",
    "video_url": "https://storage.zebracat.ai/renders/final.mp4"
  }
}
```

### `video.failed`

Fired when video generation or rendering fails.

| `data` field | Type | Description |
| ------------ | ---- | ----------- |
| `task_id` | string | The task ID returned when the video was submitted |
| `video_type` | string | One of: `idea`, `script`, `blog`, `audio`, `translate` |
| `error` | string | Human-readable error description |

```json
{
  "event": "video.failed",
  "data": {
    "task_id": "a1b2c3d4e5f6",
    "video_type": "idea",
    "error": "Rendering timed out after 30 minutes"
  }
}
```

### `project.created`

Fired when a new project is created (e.g. via a video generation request).

| `data` field | Type | Description |
| ------------ | ---- | ----------- |
| `project_id` | integer | The project ID |
| `name` | string | Project name |
| `video_type` | string | The video type used |

### `project.updated`

Fired when a project is updated.

| `data` field | Type | Description |
| ------------ | ---- | ----------- |
| `project_id` | integer | The project ID |
| `name` | string | Project name |

### `credit.low`

Fired when your API dollar balance drops below the low-balance threshold.

| `data` field | Type | Description |
| ------------ | ---- | ----------- |
| `dollar_balance` | string | Current remaining balance (e.g. `"2.50"`) |

---

## Signature verification

Every webhook request includes an `X-Webhook-Signature` header. Verify it to ensure the request came from Zebracat:

```python
import hmac, hashlib

expected = hmac.new(
    webhook_secret.encode(),
    request.body,  # raw bytes
    hashlib.sha256,
).hexdigest()

if not hmac.compare_digest(expected, request.headers['X-Webhook-Signature']):
    return HttpResponse(status=403)
```
